scope: Additional safe classroom experiment concepts only.

experiments.title: Heat and cool observation
experiments.focus: Show that water can behave differently when it is warmer or cooler.
student_observations: Temperature is a physical property.
Warm and cool liquids can behave differently.
The substance is still water.
experiments.teacher_note: Simple entry point for state and temperature ideas.

experiments.title: Melting freezing pair
experiments.focus: Pair melting with freezing to show reversible change.
student_observations: Ice can melt into liquid water.
Cooling can reverse the change in the model.
State can change while the substance stays the same.
experiments.teacher_note: Use after a basic phase-change lesson.

experiments.title: Surface behavior demo
experiments.focus: Show that a tiny amount of soap can change how water behaves at the surface.
student_observations: The surface can behave differently.
Bubbles may form more easily.
Small changes can affect physical properties.
experiments.teacher_note: Good quick demo before mixture topics.

experiments.title: Diffusion color spread
experiments.focus: Show how a colored substance can spread through water on its own.
student_observations: The color spreads without stirring in the model.
Particles move from one area to another.
Diffusion happens in everyday life too.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep the explanation visual and simple.

experiments.title: Settling sand review
experiments.focus: Show that heavier particles can settle to the bottom over time.
student_observations: Particles may move downward.
The top liquid can become clearer.
Settling is one way to separate mixtures.
experiments.teacher_note: Pairs with filtration as a comparison lesson.

experiments.title: Dilution concept
experiments.focus: Show that adding more water can make a solution less concentrated.
student_observations: The same solute can be spread through more water.
Concentration changes when more solvent is added.
Dilution does not change the identity of the solute.

experiments.title: Filtering concept 2
experiments.focus: Introduce the idea that some mixtures can be separated by filtration.
student_observations: Solid particles can be held back by a filter.
The liquid can pass through.
Filtration is a separation method.
experiments.teacher_note: Use only as a virtual concept demo.

experiments.title: Particle size effect
experiments.focus: Compare how different particle sizes look and behave in water.
student_observations: Some materials dissolve.
Some stay visible.
Particle size can affect the mixture.
experiments.teacher_note: Great for sorting and comparison activities.

experiments.title: Viscosity flow compare
experiments.focus: Compare how thick liquids flow more slowly than thin liquids.
student_observations: Some liquids flow more slowly.
Thickness is a physical property.
Viscosity can be compared in the model.

experiments.title: Evaporation rate review
experiments.focus: Show that warmer conditions can make evaporation happen faster in the model.
student_observations: Water can leave at different speeds.
Temperature can affect the rate.
Evaporation is a physical process.

experiments.title: Separation methods compare
experiments.focus: Compare layers, filtration and dissolution in one activity.
student_observations: Some mixtures separate into layers.
Some need filtration.
Some form clear solutions.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful as a revision activity for the whole unit.

experiments.title: Chromatography review
experiments.focus: Show that mixed colors can separate because different parts move differently.
student_observations: A mixed color can separate into parts.
Different components move at different speeds.
Chromatography is a separation technique.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep it as a concept lesson only.

experiments.title: Concentration strong weak
experiments.focus: Compare a stronger solution with a weaker one in the model.
student_observations: The same solute can be spread in different amounts of water.
Concentration changes the appearance of the solution.
Amount matters in a solution.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful for introducing concentration calculations later.

experiments.title: Dissolving speed compare
experiments.focus: Compare how quickly different solids dissolve in the model.
student_observations: Different solids can dissolve at different speeds.
Stirring changes the result in the model.
Rate and solubility are related but not the same.
experiments.teacher_note: A strong comparison activity for revision.

experiments.title: Dilution review
experiments.focus: Review how adding more solvent changes concentration without changing the solute.
student_observations: The same solute can become less concentrated.
Dilution changes concentration, not identity.
Concentration is about amount per volume.
experiments.teacher_note: Good as a bridge to more formal chemistry lessons.

experiments.title: Density layer comparison
experiments.focus: Show that liquids can layer depending on density and miscibility.
student_observations: Liquids may separate into layers.
Density helps explain the order.
Not all liquids mix evenly.

experiments.title: Precipitation review 3
experiments.focus: Review that some mixtures can turn cloudy because a new solid forms.
student_observations: A clear mixture can become cloudy.
A solid product can appear in the model.
Some reactions make visible products.
experiments.teacher_note: Tie this directly to the reaction registry.

experiments.title: Separation methods overview 2
experiments.focus: Review several ways to separate classroom mixtures.
student_observations: Some mixtures form layers.
Some mixtures can be filtered.
Some substances dissolve and need evaporation or crystallization.

experiments.title: Reversible changes summary
experiments.focus: Summarize which model changes are reversible and which are just state changes.
student_observations: Ice can melt and water can freeze again.
A dissolved solid can sometimes be recovered.
Some changes are easier to reverse than others.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful as a final review before assessment.
